requirements.description: The system must allow users to register with a username and password.
The system must allow registered users to log in.
The system must distinguish at least two user roles: regular user and administrator.
The system must deny access when the user does not exist, the password is incorrect, or the stated role does not match the registration.
The system must retain the identity of the logged-in user while the user navigates in the browser.
The system must display the resource-management area only to users identified as administrators.
The system must allow a user to end the session.
The system must display a home page listing the available movies.
Each listed movie must display, at a minimum, its title, poster, and rating.
The system must organize the movie listing into pages.
The system must allow the total number of registered movies to be retrieved to support paginated navigation.
The system must allow a movie-details page to be opened from the listing.
The system must provide a details page for each movie.
The details page must display, at a minimum, the title, rating, alternate title, release date, duration, director, screenplay, cast, synopsis, poster, and categories.
The system must allow the complete cast of a movie to be viewed.
The system must prevent access to the details of nonexistent movies and return an appropriate error message.
The system must provide a browsing area organized by movie categories.
The system must allow all registered categories to be viewed.
The system must allow only the movies belonging to a selected category to be listed.
A movie must be able to belong to more than one category.
The system must allow users to return from a category view to the overall catalog view.

requirements.category: Playback and access to movie files
requirements.description: The system must allow movie playback to be started from its details page.

requirements.category: Playback and access to movie files
requirements.description: The system must provide a download link for the movie file when the resource is ready for use.

requirements.category: Playback and access to movie files
requirements.description: Before playback, the system must ensure that the video file is available in the application area used to deliver content.

requirements.category: Playback and access to movie files
requirements.description: If the file is not yet available in that delivery area, the system must attempt to obtain it from the configured local repository.
An administrator must be able to register a new movie in the catalog.
Movie registration must include, at a minimum, the title, rating, alternate title, release date, duration, director, screenplay, cast, categories, synopsis, and poster.
The system must prevent duplicate registration of movies with the same title.
An administrator must be able to upload a movie video file to the application.
An administrator must be able to delete a movie from the catalog.
The system must allow more than one movie to be deleted in a batch.
Before a batch deletion, the system must inform the administrator which movies have been selected.
The system must prevent the deletion of nonexistent movies.
The system must prevent duplicate registration of users with the same username.
A movie title must be treated as the unique identifier for catalog registration.
The standard playback process assumes that the physical movie file corresponds to the registered title.
The application must be accessible through a web interface.
Catalog navigation must be simple and straightforward, with visible access to the home page, categories, details, and playback.
The application must present clear success, warning, and failure messages for key operations, including login, registration, addition, deletion, upload, and playback.
The catalog must be displayed in pages of up to 12 movies to promote visual organization and perceived performance.
The system must maintain a consistent response format for operations, indicating status, message, and returned data.
User, movie, and category information must be persistently stored.
The system must preserve the uniqueness of users and movies to prevent duplicates in the catalog and access records.
Whenever possible, error handling must return controlled messages to the user.
The system must operate with separate roles for regular users and administrators.
Catalog-management functions must be restricted to the administrator role.
The user's session must remain identified in the browser until the user logs out or clears local data.
The system must support uploads of large video files, up to 2 GB per file.
The application's operating process must treat MP4 as the standard video format.
The application environment must provide a local area to temporarily store or serve the video files used for playback.
The application environment must provide a configured local repository from which movies can be loaded on demand.
The solution must allow the user interface and the application services to evolve independently.
The user interface must be able to consume the application services even when it is deployed in a different environment.
User, movie, and category data must be stored in a structured database that supports the catalog relationships.
The system uses two types of users: regular users and administrators.
A movie can have multiple associated categories.
Uploading the video file and registering the movie are related but independent steps.
Automatic playback depends on the existence of an MP4 file corresponding to the registered title.
The source movie filename must follow the pattern expected by the environment configuration for automatic loading to work.
The intention to restrict resource management to administrators is clear in the interface, but this restriction is not fully validated in the backend.
The current system is oriented more toward a local movie catalog than toward remote storage or an external streaming service.
Availability for playback depends on both movie registration and the existence of the corresponding physical file.
